main_sand_outer.bias_notes: Left-handed (Anti-clockwise). A spacious 2,000m sand circuit featuring broad 25m wide turns and a long 460-metre home straight with a subtle +1m elevation rise from the 1200m mark to the post. Unlike tighter sand tracks, the 460m straight and slight gradient give strong-finishing stalkers ('P') and closers ('Swoopers') fair opportunities on dry sand.
main_sand_outer.post_bias: In 1200m sprints, only 236m exists before entering the sweeping turn; wide draws (10+) face a steep penalty. In 1400m and 1600m races (including the KRA Cup Mile chute), generous straightaways (446m-636m) provide one of the fairest starts in Asian racing. In 1800m races starting on the inner course, only 205m exists before the first turn—inside barriers (1–4) hold a distinct advantage.

inner_sand.bias_notes: Left-handed inner circuit used for route race starting chutes (1800m, 1900m, 2000m). Horses navigate the inner turns before transitioning to the outer track at the 1300m or 460m mark.
inner_sand.post_bias: Inside barriers (1–4) are critical due to short initial runs into the first turn before merging onto the main circuit.

handicapping_angles.moisture_content_bias_flip: Always check official KRA track moisture percentage. Moisture below 6% = deep, heavy sand that wears down leaders and rewards L400m stamina closers. Moisture above 10% = hard, fast sand that creates an extreme on-pace 'conveyor belt' favoring front-runners ('E').
handicapping_angles.spacious_460m_straight_swooper_boost: Busan's 460m home straight is 60m longer than Seoul's. Do not automatically toss deep closers on dry sand, as weak front-runners regularly hit the wall in the final 100m.
handicapping_angles.1800m_inner_start_barrier_trap: In 1800m route races (including the Korean Oaks), be cautious of wide-drawn speed horses (Barriers 8+). With only 205m to the first turn, wide runners face severe ground loss or must burn excessive fuel to cross.
handicapping_angles.kra_class_hierarchy_and_weight: In KRA Class 2-5 rating handicaps, top weights carrying 57kg+ face a strict penalty against light-weight runners (51kg-53kg) over the 460m uphill stretch (1kg = ~1 length).
handicapping_angles.seoul_vs_busan_intertrack_clash: In KRA Grade races pitting Busan against Seoul shippers (e.g., KRA Cup Mile, Korean Oaks, Owner's Cup), Busan-trained horses often possess superior early speed figures and familiarity with the 460m stretch.
